papers.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
papers.abstract: A robot world model that serves as a simulator must do more than generate plausible videos: it must faithfully follow commanded actions, maintain consistency across camera views, and sustain coherent long-horizon rollouts. We present PrimeSim, an action-conditioned, multiview world model simulator that addresses these challenges through progressive midtraining and posttraining. Starting from a pretrained video generator, we midtrain on 30,110 hours of robot demonstrations spanning 22 platforms. To improve action following, we introduce a unified cross-embodiment action representation and frame-aligned dual-path conditioning to strengthen action-frame correspondence. To maintain multiview consistency, we develop view-aware interleaved attention with explicit camera identities, enabling cross-view information exchange while preserving view-specific representations. We further introduce a fast-video, slow-memory posttraining framework that transforms the bidirectional video generator into an efficient autoregressive simulator. By combining fast causal generation, self-rollout training, and hierarchical temporal memory, PrimeSim mitigates error accumulation from self-generated histories and supports coherent long-horizon simulation. PrimeSim runs at 10.1 FPS, remains stable over long-horizon rollouts on rigid and deformable manipulation tasks, and transfers to held-out platforms within 100 to 200 gradient steps where the pretrained backbone does not. Against five open-source action-conditioned world models it leads four of the five WorldSimProbe suites and posts the best overall EWMBench score, while fine-grained local calibration still trails the field; its rollouts are faithful enough to support GRPO-based policy optimization. We release the model weights, inference code, and training code.
papers.summary_cn: PrimeSim 将 Wan2.2-TI2V-5B 视频生成器改造为动作条件、多视角、因果自回归机器人世界模型模拟器。方法分为两部分：首先利用 30,110 小时、22 个机器人平台的数据进行中期训练，通过统一的 31 维跨具身相对动作表示、帧对齐双路径动作条件和带摄像机身份的视角感知交错注意力，学习动作到多视角视觉结果的映射；随后通过分块因果建模、四步一致性蒸馏、自 rollout 分布匹配和分层 KV 时间记忆，实现快速、长时域、自条件模拟。模型可在约 10.1 FPS 下生成多视角视频，支持最长约 105 秒的连贯 rollout，并在 WorldSimProbe 和 EWMBench 上取得较强结果，还能用于在模拟器内进行 GRPO 策略优化。实验显示其具备跨平台和未见场景迁移能力，但细粒度动作校准、较高分辨率视觉保真度以及真实硬件上的闭环策略训练仍有不足或尚未验证。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 PrimeSim，一个面向机器人操作的动作条件、多视角、长时域世界模型模拟器，将预训练视频生成器转化为可交互的自回归模拟器。2. 构建涵盖 22 个机器人平台、30,110 小时示范数据的大规模跨具身中期训练框架，并提出统一跨具身动作表示和以窗口首帧为基准的相对动作块。3. 提出帧对齐双路径动作条件机制：利用帧级动作注意力建立动作—帧对应关系，并通过动作—帧适配器直接注入动作信息。4. 提出带显式摄像机身份的视角感知交错注意力，在跨视角交换信息的同时保留视角特定表示，从而提升多视角一致性。5. 提出“快速视频、慢速记忆”的后期训练框架，结合分块因果生成、四步因果一致性蒸馏、自 rollout 非对称分布匹配和分层时间记忆，缓解曝光偏差与长时域误差累积。6. 在 WorldSimProbe 五个套件中的四个套件以及 EWMBench 总体指标上取得领先，并验证模型可用于策略评估和基于 GRPO 的策略优化。
papers.relevance_cn: 该论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究动作条件视觉世界模型和闭环模拟：模型根据机器人动作预测未来多视角观测，并在自生成历史上持续 rollout。其分块因果注意力、自 rollout 训练和分层 KV-cache 记忆对应因果、流式和长视频生成；四步一致性蒸馏将 50 步采样降至 4 步，达到约 10.1 FPS，直接涉及实时生成与蒸馏加速；分层时间记忆和持久 KV-cache 则利用缓存复用支持长时域模拟。统一跨具身动作接口使模型能够迁移到不同机器人平台，闭环实验表明在 PrimeSim 中优化的策略可转移到 LIBERO 物理模拟器。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，模型每个视角的生成分辨率为 192×256，因此主要验证的是模拟器保真度、动作实现和环境响应，而非高分辨率像素级真实感。迁移到新平台仍不是零样本，需要该平台自身数据上的 100 至 200 个梯度步骤。WorldSimProbe 中的细粒度局部动作校准不如 LingBot-VA。推理速度对分辨率、预测时域和 KV-cache 长度敏感，论文报告的吞吐率并非所有模型在完全匹配的分辨率、时域和采样步数下测得。大多数定量结果以及全部闭环策略实验都来自模拟环境；论文尚未证明该模型能够在真实机器人硬件上可靠地替代模拟器用于策略改进。论文还未验证通过更长时间训练或更大数据规模能否消除平台适应需求。
papers.abstract_cn: 作为模拟器的机器人世界模型不能只生成看似合理的视频：它必须忠实遵循指定动作，保持不同摄像机视角之间的一致性，并维持长时域 rollout 的连贯性。我们提出 PrimeSim，一个通过渐进式中期训练和后期训练应对这些挑战的动作条件多视角世界模型模拟器。我们从一个预训练视频生成器出发，在涵盖 22 个平台的 30,110 小时机器人示范数据上进行中期训练。为提升动作遵循能力，我们引入统一的跨具身动作表示和帧对齐双路径条件机制，以增强动作与帧之间的对应关系。为保持多视角一致性，我们设计了带有显式摄像机身份的视角感知交错注意力，使不同视角能够交换信息，同时保留各视角特有的表示。我们进一步提出快速视频、慢速记忆的后期训练框架，将双向视频生成器转换为高效的自回归模拟器。通过结合快速因果生成、自 rollout 训练和分层时间记忆，PrimeSim 减轻了由模型自身生成历史导致的误差累积，并支持连贯的长时域模拟。PrimeSim 以 10.1 FPS 运行，在刚性和可变形物体操作任务的长时域 rollout 中保持稳定；对于预训练骨干网络无法适应的平台，它能在 100 至 200 个梯度步骤内迁移到留出平台。与五个开源动作条件世界模型相比，它在五个 WorldSimProbe 测试套件中的四个套件上领先，并取得 EWMBench 最高总体分数，但在细粒度局部校准方面仍落后于当前最佳方法；其 rollout 的保真度足以支持基于 GRPO 的策略优化。我们将发布模型权重、推理代码和训练代码。

papers.title: PlayGen2: Learning Real-Time Playable Worlds with Explicit 3D State
papers.abstract: Building a playable world requires more than generating plausible video: it demands responsive control, persistent spatial structure, and coherent interactions with dynamic entities. Using generated frames as the sole recurrent world representation ties these requirements to view-dependent appearance synthesis, making it difficult to maintain long-term spatial and temporal consistency in generation and interaction. We present PlayGen2, a real-time interactive world model that separates learned 3D state evolution from neural rendering. PlayGen2 maintains a persistent world memory comprising static geometry represented by a volumetric occupancy grid and identity-indexed 3D states for the player and other entities. Within a fixed-size local region, its world-state model jointly learns action-conditioned entity dynamics, geometry completion, and entity discovery, committing updates to a persistent world memory. A separate neural renderer synthesizes first-person observations from depth and semantic projections of the world state, without feeding generated images back into state prediction. Using Doom as a testbed, we demonstrate that the model successfully learns world dynamics including geometry-aware player motion and player--NPC interactions. The framework is computationally efficient, enabling the complete simulation and rendering pipeline to achieve approximately 160ms backend latency on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro chip. Beyond single-player interaction, we demonstrate zero-shot deployment on unseen Doom maps, multiplayer interaction through the composition of single-player models, and programmable gameplay through rule-based state interventions. These capabilities demonstrate the transferability and extensibility of the learned game-world model. Code and pretrained model weights are publicly available.
papers.summary_cn: PlayGen2提出一种面向实时可游玩世界的显式三维状态建模框架，将持久化世界状态演化与神经视频渲染解耦。模型在玩家中心的固定大小三维局部区域内，根据动作、实体历史和几何上下文，联合完成未知几何、发现新实体并预测玩家和实体的状态更新；更新后的几何与实体信息写回持久世界记忆。渲染器则利用投影得到的深度图和语义图，以及有限的 RGB 历史生成第一人称画面，生成画面不再反馈给状态预测。基于仅在单张 Freedoom2 地图上训练的 Doom 实验，模型实现了几何感知移动、玩家—NPC 交互、长时段稳定生成、未见地图零样本泛化、多人模型组合和规则化玩法干预，并在 M4 Pro 笔记本上达到约 5 FPS 的串行运行速度。
papers.contribution_cn:
1. 提出一种显式三维世界模型框架，以体素几何和按身份索引的实体状态表示世界，并在持久化世界记忆中联合学习几何补全、实体发现和动作条件动力学。
2. 将世界状态模拟与神经渲染分离，使离屏实体能够继续演化，同时减少生成视觉历史误差对状态预测的累积影响。
3. 在 Doom 上展示几何约束下的玩家运动、玩家—NPC 交互和长时域可控生成，并实现消费级笔记本上的实时交互式模拟与渲染。
4. 展示显式状态接口支持的扩展能力，包括未见地图零样本部署、单人模型组合形成多人交互，以及无需重新训练的规则式游戏状态干预。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与研究重点高度相关：它直接研究动作条件的可玩视觉世界模型和闭环交互模拟；通过持久三维状态而非纯生成帧实现长期空间一致性；通过独立状态演化和渲染环路支持因果、流式的实时生成；采用固定大小局部更新、状态缓存、RGB 历史和仅 8 步扩散去噪降低计算成本；同时涉及几何感知动力学、离屏实体持续更新、长视频 rollout、未见环境泛化及多人组合。其约 160 毫秒后端延迟、4.98 FPS 串行吞吐和重叠执行时 7.16 FPS，体现了面向实时生成的效率取向。
papers.limitations_cn: 训练数据仅来自 ViZDoom 中 Freedoom2 MAP01 的约 500 小时规则控制游戏记录，训练环境和游戏类型较为有限。实验主要集中于 Doom，模型对更复杂、更开放或真实世界场景的泛化能力尚未得到验证。渲染器生成的是学习到的 Freedoom2 风格，未见地图上的原生纹理无法由深度和语义条件直接指定，因此未见地图的参考指标会受到外观差异影响。多人交互是通过将另一名玩家表示为 Zombieman 并组合单人模型实现的，尚非经过多人数据训练的完整多人动力学。模型没有运行时碰撞修正，且部分交互规则依赖显式规则干预。实时性能仍为约 5 FPS 串行或 7.16 FPS 重叠执行，距离高帧率视频生成仍有差距。论文未明确说明在更长时间尺度、更多样动作策略或复杂实体密度下的稳定性。
papers.abstract_cn: 构建一个可游玩的世界不仅需要生成逼真的视频，还要求具备响应式控制、持久的空间结构以及与动态实体进行连贯交互的能力。若仅将生成帧作为循环世界表示，就会使这些要求依赖于视角相关的外观合成，从而难以在生成和交互过程中维持长期的空间与时间一致性。我们提出 PlayGen2，一种实时交互式世界模型，将学习到的三维状态演化与神经渲染分离。PlayGen2维护持久化世界记忆，其中静态几何由体素占据网格表示，玩家及其他实体则由按身份索引的三维状态表示。在固定大小的局部区域内，其世界状态模型联合学习动作条件下的实体动力学、几何补全和实体发现，并将更新提交到持久化世界记忆中。独立的神经渲染器根据世界状态的深度投影和语义投影合成第一人称观察，而不会将生成图像反馈到状态预测中。我们以 Doom 为测试平台，展示了该模型能够成功学习世界动力学，包括几何感知的玩家运动以及玩家与非玩家角色之间的交互。在配备 M4 Pro 芯片的 MacBook Pro 上，完整的模拟与渲染流程后端延迟约为 160 毫秒，说明该框架具有较高的计算效率。除单人交互外，我们还展示了在未见过的 Doom 地图上的零样本部署、通过组合单人模型实现多人交互，以及通过基于规则的状态干预实现可编程玩法。这些能力体现了所学习游戏世界模型的可迁移性和可扩展性。代码和预训练模型权重均已公开。

papers.title: GPWM: Modeling the World as 3D Particle Motion
papers.abstract: We introduce GPWM, a Generative Particle World Model that predicts how 3D scenes evolve by generating the motion of particles and rigid bodies over time. Unlike video world models that generate scene appearance, GPWM operates directly in 3D physical space. A single representation and architecture cover rigid, deformable, cloth, and granular materials, in both passive physics and robotic interaction. GPWM is an object-aware multi-resolution transformer that combines flow matching with diffusion forcing to generate coherent physical trajectories far beyond its training horizon. We train and evaluate GPWM on ParticleWorlds, a 25.5-million-frame corpus spanning diverse geometries, materials, interactions, and robot embodiments. GPWM outperforms the best prior learned-dynamics baseline in each of six physical domains, reducing prediction error by 31% on average. Breaking from the domain-specific setting of prior methods, a single Unified GPWM models these heterogeneous regimes with one set of weights, largely outperforming per-domain baselines and even surpassing our own specialist models in two domains. GPWM further generalizes to unseen geometries, physical properties, object counts, and rollout horizons. Beyond prediction, GPWM enables contact-rich planning by learning a generative prior over joint actuator-object motion. Instead of searching over unconstrained actions, planning searches the model's latent noise for interactions that achieve a desired object-space goal. With the same world model, noise-space planning substantially outperforms action-space search on pushing and picking, where complex contact sequences are hard to discover. Executed open-loop in simulation, the resulting plans achieve goal-directed manipulation without reference action trajectories or goal-specific policies.
papers.comment: 39 pages, 27 figures, 7 tables. Robert Ren and Matthew Bronars contributed equally (ordered by coin flip). Project page: https://robertren1122.github.io/gpwm/
papers.summary_cn: 论文提出 GPWM，一种直接在三维粒子和刚体运动空间中建模物理世界的生成式世界模型。它采用共享的粒子/刚体表示、物体感知的多分辨率时空 Transformer，以及流匹配与扩散强制，能够在多种材料、物体和机器人交互场景中生成长时域、可流式延展的物理轨迹。基于包含 2550 万帧、六类物理领域的 ParticleWorlds 数据集，GPWM 平均将预测误差降低 31%，并表现出对未见几何形状、材料参数、物体数量和更长 rollout 的泛化能力。论文还将执行器与物体轨迹联合生成，利用潜在噪声空间规划接触丰富的推动、堆料和抓取任务，在仿真开环执行中优于直接动作空间搜索。但模型依赖完整且持续跟踪的三维状态，尚未解决从原始视频进行感知和跟踪的问题；统一模型在部分领域仍逊于专用模型，长时域潜在噪声优化的计算成本也限制了在线控制。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出 GPWM，将刚体、可变形体、布料和颗粒材料统一表示为粒子运动或刚体变换，并用生成式模型预测其三维动力学。 2. 设计物体感知的多分辨率时空 Transformer，通过对象级层次化处理扩展到最多 12,000 个粒子。 3. 将流匹配与扩散强制结合，采用逐帧噪声水平和交错去噪，实现超过固定训练窗口的稳定流式、自回归生成。 4. 构建 ParticleWorlds 数据集，包含 2550 万个模拟帧，覆盖六种物理动力学、材料、几何形状、交互方式和机器人实体。 5. 在六个物理领域取得相对最强基线平均 31% 的误差降低，并展示统一模型跨异构领域训练及对未见条件和长时域的泛化能力。 6. 学习执行器—物体联合运动的生成式交互先验，在潜在噪声空间中进行规划；该方法在推动和抓取等接触丰富任务上显著优于动作空间搜索。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它不是从像素生成视频，而是直接生成三维粒子和刚体的时序运动，因此属于面向物理交互和闭环模拟的动作条件世界模型。模型可接收未来执行器运动作为条件，也可联合生成执行器与物体轨迹，并通过物体空间目标反向引导潜在噪声，从而完成接触丰富的目标导向规划。其扩散强制机制允许近未来逐步确定、远未来保持可修改，并通过固定窗口流式延展到远超训练长度的 rollout，直接对应自回归、因果/流式和长视频（长时域）生成方向。多分辨率注意力降低了密集粒子场景的计算负担，生成先验也为闭环控制和模拟中的策略搜索提供了结构化轨迹分布。不过，论文主要处理已获得的三维跟踪状态，并未实现从 RGB/RGB-D 视频端到端构建视觉世界模型，因此与视频扩散外观生成的关联是间接的。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出以下局限：第一，GPWM 假设能够获得完整且持续跟踪的三维场景状态，实验将物理预测与感知分离，尚未解决从原始视觉观测中恢复持久粒子和物体身份的问题。第二，尽管 Unified GPWM 可以用一组权重建模异构物理领域，但在部分设置中仍落后于领域专用模型，显示出领域间干扰和专业化差距。第三，潜在噪声优化需要对完整生成过程求导；长时域任务还需跨多个流式窗口反向传播，因此计算成本随规划时域增长，目前限制了快速在线控制。论文未明确说明真实世界闭环机器人部署中的性能和鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_cn: 我们提出 GPWM，即生成式粒子世界模型，通过生成粒子和刚体随时间的运动来预测三维场景如何演化。不同于生成场景外观的视频世界模型，GPWM 直接在三维物理空间中运行。单一的表示和架构覆盖刚体、可变形体、布料和颗粒材料，既适用于被动物理过程，也适用于机器人交互。GPWM 是一种具备物体感知能力的多分辨率 Transformer，将流匹配与扩散强制相结合，从而生成远超训练时域的连贯物理轨迹。我们在 ParticleWorlds 上训练和评估 GPWM。该数据集包含 2550 万帧，涵盖多样的几何形状、材料、交互方式和机器人实体。在六个物理领域中，GPWM 均优于此前最佳的学习动力学基线，平均将预测误差降低 31%。不同于以往方法针对特定领域建模的设定，单一的 Unified GPWM 使用一组权重对这些异构物理状态进行建模，其性能大幅超过各领域基线，并且在两个领域中甚至超过我们自己的专用模型。GPWM 还能够泛化到未见过的几何形状、物理属性、物体数量和 rollout 时域。除预测之外，GPWM 还通过学习联合执行器—物体运动的生成式先验，实现接触丰富的规划。规划不再搜索不受约束的动作，而是搜索模型的潜在噪声，以找到能够实现目标物体空间状态的交互过程。在推动和抓取任务中，这类噪声空间规划显著优于动作空间搜索，因为复杂的接触序列很难被发现。最终得到的规划在仿真中以开环方式执行，无需参考动作轨迹或任务特定策略即可实现目标导向的操作。

papers.title: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk and have made efficient video generation practical. However, further accelerating these models toward real-time generation remains challenging, as few-step distillation leaves little cross-step redundancy for existing training-free caching methods to exploit. We revisit this regime and identify two token-level redundancy patterns: cross-frame redundancy from static content shared across adjacent frames, and cross-step redundancy from tokens that converge early during denoising. Crucially, we find that early clean estimates along the model's own denoising trajectory provide an effective online signal for locating both patterns, requiring no retraining, auxiliary predictor, or reference video. Based on these findings, we propose PreSTP (Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning), a training-free framework that constructs a unified token-wise redundancy mask from cross-frame similarity and cross-step convergence. Tokens marked as redundant skip subsequent computation under a consistent last-computed-value restoration rule, and a content-adaptive mask reuse strategy further reduces dense probing cost. On 5-second generation, PreSTP achieves 1.52x-3.20x speedups and a better efficiency-fidelity trade-off than coarse-grained caching baselines such as TeaCache and FlowCache. On 30-second generation, it reaches up to 1.96x speedup while improving VBench-Long and suppressing long-horizon drift. Notably, it continues to reduce inference cost even in the extreme one-step regime, where cross-step redundancy vanishes entirely and coarse step-wise caching is no longer applicable.

papers.title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
papers.abstract: Conversational video characters must generate video as fast as it plays, for one user at a time: at 24 fps, a sustained 166.7 ms per four-frame chunk at batch size one, with only a few chunks of buffering. We describe the system behind Runway Characters, which serves a $\approx$57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer (four denoising passes per chunk) at 704$\times$1088 and 24 fps on four H100 GPUs with a voice agent in the loop. Each chunk takes 240 attention calls, each reading a 5,788-slot KV cache in which only 757 tokens are new, and 29% of the original step was whole-cache work repeated in every call. We move that work to write time (a ring cache, RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, and a delta rotation when positions reset), fuse the tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM with in-switch reduction, and give the decoder that turns latents into video frames its own GPU. Without the fused kernel, our optimizations cut the diffusion step from 240.9 to 159.3 ms (1.51$\times$, 24.5 fps sustained) with no detected degradation in lip-sync scores; the fused kernel, rolled back once in production and since re-enabled, reaches 147.4 ms (1.63$\times$, 43% of FP8 peak). In seven weeks of production the worker averaged above 23.5 fps in 99.5% of sessions that streamed for at least a second, and our pipeline takes 0.49 s of a 2.1 s median conversational turn. On the same GPUs, the two open-source real-time video systems we benchmarked, at four denoising passes, miss real time or add over a second of latency (one by estimate), at a third to half of our resolution.

papers.title: Learning Robotic World Models with Semantic and Visual Feedback
papers.abstract: Robot world models predict action-conditioned future visual states to support robotic planning and decision making. However, visual reconstruction does not fully capture task progress, semantic evaluation alone provides limited constraints on fine-grained visual errors, and homogeneous predictions limit comparative feedback. We present RoboImagine, a framework for post-training autoregressive robotic world models through candidate-future comparisons with semantic and visual feedback. Diverse search promotes diversity among candidate trajectories under shared visual observations, action sequences, and task instructions. A frozen multimodal evaluator provides task-relevant semantic preferences through pairwise video comparisons in both presentation orders, complemented by pixel- and perceptual-level visual consistency feedback that constrains local structural and appearance errors. These signals drive policy optimization through group-relative advantages. Fixed initial context and branch-specific rolling histories support long-sequence generation with bounded context and consistent conditioning between candidate generation and policy optimization. Experiments with separately trained models on RT-1, BridgeV2, and RoboCasa cover real-world and simulated manipulation. On RT-1, under matched initialization, update counts, and evaluation protocols, RoboImagine improves PSNR by 1.26 dB and reduces LPIPS by 11.93% relative to continued supervised fine-tuning. Ablations show that diverse search improves prediction quality and that combined semantic and visual feedback yields higher external multimodal evaluation scores than visual feedback alone while maintaining comparable visual fidelity. Rolling histories further improve long-horizon prediction. These results support improving visual fidelity, task relevance, and long-horizon prediction through candidate comparison and complementary feedback.

papers.title: Future Representation Distillation for Imagination-free World Action Models
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) use the predictive knowledge of pretrained video diffusion models for robot control through future video prediction. However, iterative video denoising is costly, and inaccurate visual predictions can compromise action prediction. Our key idea is to make this predictive knowledge available through visual representations computed from the current observation, enabling action prediction without generating future videos. We introduce DreamFree, a WAM that repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a predictive visual encoder through representation distillation. The visual encoder learns to predict a frozen video diffusion model's representation using only the current observation. An action module is then trained to predict actions by extracting action-relevant information from the visual encoder. Across real-world and simulated tasks, DreamFree achieves higher success rates than state-of-the-art VLAs and WAMs, while performing real-time closed-loop control at 11Hz with a 14B video diffusion backbone. Experiments show that DreamFree can translate stronger video priors and additional video data into better robot control and enable learning new robot tasks from video demonstrations, including videos from a different embodiment, without action annotation for the new tasks.

papers.title: TouchéWorld tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds
papers.abstract: Recent video world models allow users to explore generated environments through camera navigation. Continuous hand motion provides a fine-grained action channel for interacting with the people and objects encountered during exploration. We present TouchéWorld, a framework that integrates gesture-driven interaction into a camera-controlled video world model. Given an initial image and a scene-description prompt, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. We construct joint camera--hand training data from heterogeneous egocentric videos through annotation completion, consistency-based filtering, and temporal alignment. Building on a pretrained camera-controlled world model, we combine spatial hand-skeleton conditioning with numerical hand-motion features through parameter-efficient adaptation. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation support chunk-level online generation, allowing users to update their controls based on generated visual feedback. We further introduce TouchéBench to evaluate hand-motion following, camera--hand coordination, online interaction, and object response. Together, these components establish a framework for studying continuous exploration and hand-driven interaction within generative worlds.

papers.title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
papers.abstract: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.

papers.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes
papers.abstract: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause. World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy. The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner. We pair a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, one for nearby social dynamics and one for future scene semantics, that score candidate actions by their predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy acts in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, this yields navigation that is simultaneously safer, more socially and group-coherent, and more goal-directed than strong reactive and learned baselines, with naive observers rating the resulting motion as more human-like. Taken together, our findings point to a different approach for bringing world-model foresight into deployable agents: not accelerating rollouts, but amortizing them into the policy so that the cost of looking ahead is confined to training. Project page: https://seoneun.github.io/-NeurIPS-2026-Seeing-Beyond-the-Next-Step/
